I'm glad this is considered a bug by the pytorch maintainers, but at risk of sounding pedantic, doesn't this fall under https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html#linear-algebra-torch-linalg (extremal values) for which Pytorch provides no guarantees '..the result of these functions they may vary when using the same inputs on different devices...'? There are a large number of Pytorch operations that currently return inconsistent behavior on singular matrices.

The next part of the statement from the numerical accuracy docs says:
```
"... when the inputs have non-finite values like inf or NaN"
```

In this case, inputs are all non-inf and non-NaN. The docs for `logdet()` explicitly say it will return -inf for inputs with determinant == 0 so to me this reads as a GPU-side correctness issue.

My interpretation was more along the lines that `logdet` as a matrix function is ill-conditioned (infinite condition number) about singular matrix inputs. But if the specific API method docs are a source of truth for the expected behavior, this is great.
Put up a fix here https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/157910
Looks like the PR intended to fix this didn't get merged in (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/157910#issuecomment-3064368647)?
I would like to research on this.

This should be fixed by #171305 (which addresses the same root cause as #170834). The `Generated` class in `_library/autograd.py` now uses `_SingleLevelFunction` which bypasses the functorch check in `Function.apply()`.

Thank you for investigating!

Also, how do I make torch.compile artifacts be cached across runs? With regular PyTorch (not vllm) my small language model takes a few minutes to torch.compile, and this happens every run (there is 1 recompile as well, but not more, so no hidden recompiles draining the time). So cache is not hit. Is there a way to force PyTorch to store torch.compile artifacts? 

`TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE=1` doesn't help: it forces the recompile to hit the cache, but the first run still takes a few minutes
Would be great to have a tlparse

I'll add repro script for PyTorch case - but it's very basic, just load a HF model, and do a few forward passes

But same for vllm, simply running serve command always takes up 1 minute or more in compile stage

E.g. even this prints 15-30 seconds at every run - meaning just torch.compile / graph capture takes 15-30 seconds (e.g. `PleIAs/Monad` takes ~30 seconds every time just for torch.compile):

```python
mport os; os.environ.update(dict(TORCHINDCUTOR_CACHE_DIR = '.cache', TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE='1', TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOGRAD_CACHE='1', TORCH_LOGS = 'recompiles'))
import time
import torch
import transformers

class Model(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.llm = transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            'Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B',
            attn_implementation = 'sdpa',
            dtype = torch.bfloat16,
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        outputs = self.llm.model(
            inputs_embeds=x,
            attention_mask=torch.ones(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], dtype=torch.long, device=x.device),
            return_dict=True,
        )
        return outputs.last_hidden_state.sum()

@torch.compile(fullgraph=True)
def compute_output(f, x):
    return f(x)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print(transformers.__version__, torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.backends.cudnn.version())

    model = Model().to('cuda')
    x = torch.zeros((64, 145, 1024), device = 'cuda', dtype = torch.bfloat16)
    tic = time.time()
    a = compute_output(model, x)
    print(time.time() - tic)

    tic = time.time()
    a = compute_output(model, x)
    print(time.time() - tic)
```

If it's FX transformations taking so much time, couldn't torch.compile somehow hash at disk the original graph and retrieve the transformed graph? Or is it the initial graph capture that's so slow?

It would be not perfectly satisfactory, but is it possible to at least manually cache the captured graph? E.g. to quick-start the model instantly by loading the graph (with tensors on meta-devices) from disk (and then loading weights into it)?

@vadimkantorov This is two separate issues, right? (1) A feature request for shared compile artifacts and (2) a caching issue? If so it really should be filed separately so we can address them separately.

I guess it depends on how sharing between processes/ranks is implemented :) If it's implemented via caching - then maybe it's the same issue (could also be slightly related to [the new Precompile feature](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/171301) which allows saving/loading compilation artifact to/from file)

Some related comments from the vllm discussion, cc @zou3519 :
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/18851#issuecomment-3656916310
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/18851#issuecomment-3656869499

---

So maybe this issue is solved by testing if compile artifacts can be shared between processes/machines/ranks via MegaCache (or cache via a shared NFS/S3 dir, and not force using a Redis server) and by making sure that the graph capture / cache key calculation itself is fast and does not take 15-30-60 seconds by itself (before even cache is looked up). There needs to be a way to have a fast mode of cache key calculation (based on source code hash or config or sth like that), at least for HF models somehow

Right now pytorch is specializing on
(a) the device ID
(b) the collective target name
(c) DTensor slicing by rank.
these specializations result in a different output graph on every rank. So you should be seeing caching on the same rank across runs but you won't get caching between ranks because the ranks have different outputs (because of this specialization).

(a) is addressed in torchrun via https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/166680. Other runners (vllm, for example) will need to do a similar change if they want that same behavior.

(b) and (c) are addressed by a series of PRs that I'm working on now such that with all three of these all the ranks should output the same graph/code for all ranks.

That should help the initial request. If you're not seeing any caching from run to run that won't be helped by my fixes.

about (a) - I wonder if it could be made more explicit - as some arg to torch.compile? it's quite surprising that it's specializing on based on `LOCAL_RANK` env var... and by device ID - does you mean integer device index or some device guid?

And also in general - can the user access the computed cache key to debug these issues?

---

And about the repro above - why is it taking 15-30 seconds for torch.compile of a simple model on a single gpu above? (even if caching is switched on) Is the time spent on initial Dynamo capturing? or on graph transformations? Is it possible to also do some ultra-fast cache key computation e.g. by hashing source code of the model (or even forcing the user to specify which files to key on)? At least for HF models, there should be some very fast way to do this (e.g. by some config or model version sha, transformers library commit sha), as we keep capturing the same graphs all over again and spending minutes on this on every run

---

And also a question about:
- does it work correctly on NFS-d / networked directories as cache location?
- is there any support for S3 directory instead of Redis / file system? it could be done via fsspec (in the simplest case), related: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/155992
- Must I enable any of these TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE='1', TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOGRAD_CACHE='1'? it would be nice to have max. caching by default

re (1) with the approach we're using (tweaking CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) it has to be set before cuda is loaded during `import torch`. There's a longer-term approach where instead we treat the deviceId as an input into the function (instead of being specialized) but that's lo-priority since we have a work-around for now.

I haven't had time to look at your repro to debug timing yet. Generally we see long compile times on simple models when they have large loops which get unrolled. Using hierarchical compilation might help - see https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compiler.nested_compile_region.html.

We don't currently cache the initial dynamo trace - the caching is at the autograd/inductor layer so maybe that's why you're not seeing a lot of caching help. Precompile should help in that regard (and all the other max caching issues as well).

I'm not as familiar with the cache stuff. We definitely can debug the cache stuff internally but I'm not sure how much OSS support is there. So I also can't answer your other cache questions - but I'd be worried about consistency on an NFS mount.

Yeah, probably some aggressive caching needs to be offered at Dynamo level - to target the basic usecase of compiling HF models whose source code do not change all the time. So some variant of reliable computing of key (from HF model itself and maybe torch.compile options) and then looking up the artifacts is needed. I also wonder if torch.compile options can be incorporated in the cache key in some easy way, because it seems that any torch.compile options are global, and can be overridden by any subsequent or enclosing torch.compile call.

And the usecase of supporting reliably NFS / networked fs and S3 as cache locations would be very nice for academic/small cluster settings

I found a critical condition for reproducing this issue. The crash only occurs when **`torch.set_default_device()`** or a **`with torch.device(...):`** context is active.

It seems that setting a global default device confuses the compiler regarding the tensor's placement, leading it to generate a CPU kernel for a tensor that actually resides on the device (e.g., CUDA).

If I remove the default device context, `torch.compile` works correctly.
